cards.text: Jesus is still sitting on the Mount of Olives, answering His disciples' question about the sign of His coming and the end of the age (Matthew 24:3). Now He gives them something to watch for: "the abomination of desolation," spoken of by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place. Then comes a quick note right in the middle: let the reader understand.

cards.question: When they see the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place, Jesus says those in Judea should flee to the ___.

cards.text: There's NO time to pack. Whoever's up on the housetop shouldn't even come down to grab anything from the house, and friend, I'm the guy who goes back in three times for my keys.

cards.question: Jesus says the person out working in the field can run home for their cloak first.
With those in Judea fleeing to the mountains, Jesus says, "How miserable those days will be" for which people?

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them to pray about when that run will happen.

cards.question: Jesus tells them to pray that their flight to the mountains won't happen in which season?

cards.text: Not in winter, and not on the Sabbath either. Then Jesus says why: at that time there will be great tribulation.

cards.question: Jesus says a tribulation like this one has never been seen since the beginning of the world.

cards.text: That's heavy, friend. Jesus says that if those days kept going, nobody would be saved.

cards.question: For the sake of the elect, what does Jesus say will happen to those days of tribulation?

cards.text: Next, Jesus brings up what to do at that time if anyone tells them, 'Look, here is the Christ!' or 'There He is!'

cards.question: If anyone says, "Look, here is the Christ!" what does Jesus tell His disciples to do?

cards.text: Here's why: false Christs and false prophets will appear. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer believing an expired coupon that SWORE it was still good, so I'm listening REAL close to this part.

cards.question: Jesus says these false Christs and false prophets will perform great signs and wonders.
Jesus says the false Christs and false prophets will try to deceive someone, if that were possible. Who?

cards.text: Jesus says, "See, I have told you in advance." So if anyone says He's out in the wilderness, don't go, and if they say He's in the inner rooms, don't believe it.

cards.question: Instead, Jesus says the coming of the Son of Man will be like something that comes from the east and flashes as far as the west. What is it?

cards.text: Lightning doesn't need a group chat to announce it, friend. Then Jesus adds a short saying: "Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather."
Then Jesus says what comes immediately after the tribulation of those days: the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.

cards.question: With the sun darkened and the moon giving no light, Jesus says the stars will ___ from the sky.

cards.text: And the powers of the heavens will be shaken. At that time, the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn.

cards.question: Then all the tribes of the earth will see the Son of Man coming. How does Jesus say He will come?

cards.text: With power and great glory, friend. And then comes a loud trumpet call.

cards.question: With a loud trumpet call, who does the Son of Man send out?
Jesus says the angels will gather His elect from only one place on earth.

cards.text: Now Jesus gives them a lesson from the fig tree: watch for its branches to turn tender and sprout leaves. Friend, my oven gives me zero heads-up; it goes straight from almost to BURNT.

cards.question: When the fig tree's branches turn tender and sprout leaves, what does Jesus say you know is near?
Jesus says it's the same when they see all these things. How near does He say He is?

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened."

cards.question: Jesus says heaven and earth will pass away, but His ___ will never pass away.

cards.text: Heaven and earth can go, and His words are still standing. And friend, Jesus isn't done teaching on that mountain yet, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: Matthew 24:21 also says this tribulation will be 'never to be seen again.' No card tells this. Card 8 only says there will be great tribulation, and card 9 only covers 'since the beginning of the world.' The baker leaves without half of the verse's claim.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Even the elect' stands out. Both wrong answers start with 'Only' ('Only the Pharisees', 'Only the Gentiles'). With 'if that were possible' in the question, the one answer that doesn't start with 'Only' is the obvious pick.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: This is the first time the Son of Man appears, and no card says who He is. The baker isn't told that this is the title Jesus uses for Himself, for example in Matthew 16:13. Cards 12, 14 and 15 then ask about the Son of Man and 'His elect' with no link to Jesus.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card carries three separate things: the powers of the heavens are shaken, the sign of the Son of Man appears in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth mourn.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Card 6 already told the baker not to believe anyone who says He's in the inner rooms. That rules out the wrong answer 'Into the inner rooms' before the question is asked, so only two answers are really in play.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No card tells where the elect are gathered from: 'from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other' (Matthew 24:31). The true or false card only shows it isn't one place, so the baker never sees the actual picture.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Just past the hills' also means very near, close to the right answer 'Right at the door.' After being told 'it's the same' as summer being near, a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This blank asks the baker to supply the wording of the line ('His ___ will never pass away'). Nothing on the earlier cards lets a baker reason out 'words' over 'temple' or 'city.' It tests wording they haven't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'Heaven and earth can go, and His words are still standing,' only restates the answer to card 5 and covers no new part of the passage. Since verse 35 was asked on a choice card, this card can be just the 'story isn't over' line.
